newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Estate Mortgage lawsuit in Australian court.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Estate Mortgage lawsuit in Australian court.

text.p: Litigation over the A$600 million collapse of the Estate Mortgage Trusts began in the Victorian Supreme Court in Melbourne on Monday.

The trial, which is expected to run for nine to 12 months sees Trustees of Estate Mortgage, now renamed Meridian Investment Trust, pitted against nine defendants, including food ingredients group Burns Philp & Co Ltd.
According to defence documents prepared by Burns Philp, its subsidiary Burns Philp Trustee Co (BPTC) was the Estate Mortgage trustee from 1983 until it went into liquidation in 1990.
"In 1990 the (Estate Mortgage) Trusts experienced a cash crisis and were unable to make income distibutions or to meet unit holders' requests for redemption of units," Burns Philp said.
The collapse left about 50,000 investors with A$600 million in losses.

Meridian Trustees John Murphy and Peter Allen of Arthur Andersen are seeking to prove Burns Philp was a "shadow director" of BPTC and therefore liable for losses suffered in relation to 13 mortgage loans.

If the actions are successful, the defendants may have to meet claims of up to A$722 million, depending on interest caclulations and from what point in time defendants might be regarded as having been at fault.

"BPC (Burns Philp) is of the view that the plaintiffs will be unable to produce evidence to show that the directors of BPTC were 'accustimed to act in accordance with BPC's directions or instructions' which the plaintiffs must prove in order to show that BPC was a 'shadow director'," Burns Philp said.
Burns Philp shares closed up one cent at A$2.25.
